source.title: Layer-Aware Representation Filtering: Purifying Finetuning Data to Preserve LLM Safety Alignment
source.authors: Hao Li; Lijun Li; Zhenghao Lu; Xian Wei; Rui Li; Jing Shao; Lei Sha

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning can raise harmful compliance, using LARF-ranked benign subsets and ASR rather than the original study's method. Also tests layer sensitivity by scaling layer parameters and measuring refusals.
record.gate_note: The reported fine-tuning ASRs and parameter-scaling refusal results are included. Cited results from other work are not included. The paper also reports comparisons with SEAL, GradSafe and Bi-Anchoring, downstream-task safety results, and other analyses; these are omitted under the row limit.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama3-8B, Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B instruct models on benign Alpaca and Dolly subsets. It uses 1,000 random samples (3-run mean), the 1,000 highest-scoring and the 1,000 lowest-scoring samples by LARF, and measures LlamaGuard ASR on DirectHarm4, HarmBench and HEx-PHI against the instruct model. This bears directly on V2. The method differs from the original: LoRA, 1,000-sample subsets and a LlamaGuard judge. The layer-scaling experiment is a selection step for the authors' own filter, not a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign datasets contain hard-to-spot safety-degrading samples, typically long point-by-point responses, that compromise alignment when fine-tuned on. They conclude that LARF identifies these samples efficiently via representations at a safety-sensitive layer, and that removing them mitigates degradation without hurting utility. They note filtering alone cannot fully prevent degradation. The 'not a first-token account' clause is the reader's gloss, not the authors' statement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses representation ranking to select benign training examples, then measures safety after fine-tuning; the layer-sensitivity experiment scales layer parameters rather than measuring per-token KL or applying the original claim's interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with ranked subset (highest versus lowest safety-degrading scores), random versus ranked sampling, training dataset, model, and evaluation benchmark. Identified sensitive layer varies by model.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling a single layer's attention and FFN weights by 1±α shifts refusal counts on a 110-prompt over-refusal set most strongly at one mid-depth layer per model. The maximum normalized change rate ranges from k=140 to 370, at layer 13 for Llama3/3.1, 18 for Qwen2.5, 25 for Qwen2, 16 for Mistral-v0.2 and 21 for Phi-3-mini. Data selected by that layer's representations yields the highest post-fine-tuning ASR (Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal sensitivity to weight scaling is concentrated in an identifiable mid-depth 'safety-sensitive layer'.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The layer-scaling experiment's individual refusal counts are mainly shown in figures; the text gives a directional description for Llama3 and maximum sensitivity scores for several models. ASR uncertainty is not reported; the random baseline is averaged across three runs without a reported dispersion measure. The overrejection calibration set has 110 instructions.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted Table 1 and Table 5 comparator-method results for SEAL, GradSafe and Bi-Anchoring, and Table 2 downstream-task safety results for filtered datasets. Also omitted layer-by-layer figure values and the representation, similarity, and data-character analyses. Kept the full reported random/LARF-high/LARF-low ASR set for Alpaca and Dolly (Tables 1 and 5) and the stated selected-layer sensitivity results (Section 4.2 and Appendix D.2).

untested.parts: Only 1,000-sample LoRA (rank 8) subsets of Alpaca and Dolly in the main rows. Full-dataset and full-parameter fine-tuning are not tested, and example count is not varied.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis. Shallow alignment is only cited when critiquing Bi-Anchoring's first-10-token gradients.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
The layer-scaling experiment only selects a layer for data filtering, using over-refusal counts. It does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour on harmful prompts.
Not tested. Point-style, long-response features of degrading data are offered as a hypothesis about which benign data erodes safety, not about first-token shallowness.

missing.what: Random-baseline downstream fine-tuning (10k Magicoder/PubMedQA/MetaMath) gives GPT-4o-judged DirectHarm4 ASR of 14.5–37.5%. This bears on V2 for ordinary task data. The instruct baseline was not re-measured with the GPT-4o judge.
Larger models (Llama3-70B, Qwen2.5-32B/72B) fine-tuned on random PubMedQA show GPT ASR of 26.25–56.5%. No instruct baseline is reported.
Category breakdown: top-ranked fine-tuning raises ASR for content-generation topics (adult content, political campaigning, disinformation, phishing) but not for physical harm or illegal activities.

record.verdict_notes: Main-text naming is inconsistent: the abstract and intro call the degrading subset 'bottom ranked', while Section 4 and the tables call it 'top ranked'. Rows follow the tables. No uncertainty is reported for any ASR, and random results are a 3-run mean without dispersion. The study is not an original source. Its V2 evidence includes both ordinary (random) and selected benign data, with strong dataset dependence: Dolly erodes safety far more than Alpaca at 1,000 samples.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fine-tuning on selected 1,000-example subsets and random 1,000-example subsets from Alpaca and Dolly, not the full range of ordinary or carefully chosen benign datasets or example counts.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
Scales layer attention and feed-forward parameters; does not isolate a small individual weight set or rank.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety beyond the first tokens.

rows.subject: Llama3
rows.operation_detail: Scale each layer's attention and feed-forward parameters by 1 ± α and measure refusal-count sensitivity.
rows.note: The text says weakening this layer greatly reduces refusals and strengthening it greatly increases refusals; the reported k is the highest normalized change rate.
rows.check: k=370 is the argmax selection value LARF uses to pick a layer. It is measured on 110 over-refusal prompts, has no baseline and is not a rate of harmful compliance. It localizes to a whole layer, not a small weight set or rank.

rows.subject: Llama3.1
rows.operation_detail: Scale layer parameters and select the layer with maximum refusal-count sensitivity.
rows.note: The appendix reports the selected layer and maximum k; individual refusal counts are not given in text.

labels.reason: Table 1 shows increased ASR for all three models on both benchmarks, including 11.25→25.00% and 3.50→18.50% (r01,r04,r19,r22,r37,r40).

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Random Alpaca fine-tuning evaluated on HEx-PHI
labels.reason: The model group mixes small increases, 5.86→8.97% and 9.66→13.10%, with a decrease, 8.62→6.55% (r25,r43,r07).

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Benign subsets with the lowest LARF scores (short, non-point-style responses)
labels.reason: Table 5 shows lower ASR in 16 of 18 conditions; Qwen2.5/Dolly increases on DirectHarm4 and Harmbench. The mixed group establishes selection dependence (including r03,r24,r48,r51).

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Random Alpaca fine-tuning of Llama3, HEx-PHI
labels.reason: ASR decreases from 8.62% to 6.55%, opposite to V2 in this tested condition (r07); dispersion is not reported.

relation.reason: Tables 1 and 5 directly measure safety changes after benign fine-tuning against instruct baselines.

tranche.reason: Representation-based benign-data selection followed by fine-tuning and harmful-response measurement tests V2 through a different method.

source_check.notes: Random ASRs average three runs without reported dispersion. The introduction inconsistently names top/bottom ranks; the score formula, Section 4.3.2, and Tables 1 and 5 support the recorded highest-/lowest-score interpretation.

statements.correction: Table 1: highest-score subsets ASR 26.21–86.50%; instruct baselines 3.50–13.25%. Sections 4.3.1–4.3.2: 1,000-example subsets and random controls. Appendix C.5: rank-8 LoRA. Table 2: utility checks. Abstract: code link. Review status: unverified from supplied text.
statements.problem: The experimental claims match, with 26% rounding the minimum 26.21%; reviewed status cannot be established from the supplied study text.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 highest safety-degrading-score samples across the tested models, datasets and benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: ASR rises substantially from the instruct baselines in the reported top-ranked conditions (r02, r05, r08, r11, r14, r17, r20, r23, r26, r29, r32, r35, r38, r41, r44, r47, r50, r53).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 lowest-ranked samples and random samples
reader_labels.reason: Low-ranked subsets generally reduce ASR, while random-sample outcomes vary in magnitude; increases are not uniform across conditions (r01-r54).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Random Alpaca fine-tuning of Llama3 on HEx-PHI
reader_labels.reason: ASR is lower than the instruct reference rather than raised (r07).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Layer-wise parameter scaling on the overrejection dataset
reader_labels.reason: The reported maximal refusal-count sensitivity identifies a layer in each tested model, and the text explicitly describes refusal shifts for Llama3 (r55-r60).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The results localize sensitivity to a layer, but do not establish that a small individual weight set or rank carries safety behaviour (r55-r60).
